arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Cooper's lawyer argued the bad advice caused a much longer prison term.
The state's lawyer argued the trial itself was fair and reliable.
The state's lawyer argued a new trial is the standard remedy for bad advice.
Justice Kagan questioned why a longer sentence is not a different outcome.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Cooper rejected a plea deal after his lawyer advised him to. He lost at trial and received a harsher sentence. He argues this bad advice violated his rights. The state argues the trial itself was fair and reliable.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the scope of the right to effective counsel during plea negotiations. It determines whether a longer sentence from a rejected deal counts as legal harm. The outcome shapes how courts evaluate claims of bad legal advice in criminal cases.
